item.title: Man dies after serious assault in Ballaghaderreen
item.description: A man has died following a serious assault in Ballaghaderreen, County Roscommon. It happened on Barrack Street at around 1am on New Year's Day. A man in his 30s was taken to Beaumont Hospital in a critical condition - Gardaí have this morning confirmed he has since passed away. Advertisement A man in his 40s has been charged in connection with the investigation. He is due to appear before Roscommon District Court this morning. Gardaí say investigations are ongoing.

item.title: N5 bypass to be "game-changer" for West of Ireland
item.description: The N5 Ballaghaderreen to Scramogue bypass is set to be a game-changer for the West of Ireland. That's according to Roscommon County Council Chief Executive Shane Tiernan. The 34-kilometre stretch of road will bypass Frenchpark, Ballinagare, Tulsk and Strokestown. Advertisement Tiernan says some of the new road may be opened next year.

item.title: Status yellow snow and ice warnings extended across Shannonside region
item.description: Weather warnings have been extended across the Shannonside region, with temperatures set to barely rise above zero today. A low of minus 6 point 8 degrees was recorded overnight, and snow has fallen in parts of the north-west. A status yellow snow-ice alert for all of Connacht along with Donegal, Cavan, Monaghan and Louth will remain in place until 11 o'clock tomorrow morning. item.description: A Ukrainian man has been charged with assault causing serious harm in connection with the death of a man following an incident in Ballaghaderreen in the early hours of New Year's Day. item.title: Roscommon Council teams up to enhance National Famine Way
item.description: Roscommon County Council are currently in collaboration with seven other local authorities to enhance the National Famine Way. The National Famine Way runs from Strokestown to the docks in Dublin. Council Chief Executive Shane Tiernan says it's an exciting project. Advertisement

item.title: Live Updates: St. Brigids v Scotstown
item.description: Follow live updates of the All-Ireland club football semi-final as St. Brigid's face Scotstown. Connacht champions Brigid's were All-Ireland champions in 2013 and runners up in 2024. Whereas, Ulster champions Scotstown are back at this stage for the first time since 1989. Throw-in at Kingspan Breffni is 3pm. Advertisement

item.title: Man named following fatal collision in Longford
item.description: The man who died in last night’s fatal road collision in Longford has been identified. He has been named locally as 36-year-old Francis Kelly with an address in County Longford. This marks the first road fatality in Ireland this year. Advertisement The crash occurred in Edgeworthstown at about 7 o'clock yesterday evening, when two cars and a van collided on the N4. item.title: Irish hot air balloon experts set for Lough Key Forest Park in 2026
item.description: Hot-air balloon experts from across the world will once again descend on Lough Key Forest Park in Boyle in 2026. That's after it was confirmed in December that The Irish Hot Air Ballooning Championships will take place there next September. Thousands of people watched the experts earlier this year with photos going viral on social media. Advertisement The 2026 Championships will take place between the 19th and 25th September. Event director Frank Meldon is looking forward to returning to Boyle.

item.title: 'It's just devastating' - Glowing tributes to Longford dad who died in crash
item.description: Tributes are being paid to the young Longford father who died in a crash at the weekend. Francis Kelly lost his life in a three-vehicle crash between Longford town and Edgeworthstown on Saturday at around 7pm. The 36-year-old is the first person to die on Irish roads this year.
